approach: Keep the current DOM/CSS CRT shell and exact historical visual timing, then refactor only the browser-local row/line reveal into an explicit controller. A capture-phase key guard completes the current visible reveal and consumes that physical key while preserving all persistent effects, authoritative state, and current architecture.

decisions.decision: Retain exact historical DOM/CSS CRT effects with no reduced-motion branch
decisions.why: The clarified product contract requires the historical palette and persistent motion to remain active
decisions.rejected: OS or application motion preferences and a rendering redesign

decisions.decision: Use an idempotent generation-safe reveal controller
decisions.why: It can complete remaining nodes synchronously and prevent stale callbacks after replacement
decisions.rejected: Timer-only state or a persistent skip flag

decisions.decision: Consume the reveal-skip key before normal input and suppress same-press repeats until keyup
decisions.why: The physical key used to skip must cause zero normal terminal actions
decisions.rejected: Continuing dispatch or swallowing later input for a timeout

decisions.decision: Keep pagination and layout recalculation immediate for already-opened content
decisions.why: Content identity, not page fitting, owns reveal replay under FR-010 and FR-011
decisions.rejected: Revealing every pagination or resize result

decisions.decision: Separate temporal assertions from stable historical-color snapshots
decisions.why: Frozen screenshots protect exact visual states while browser animation data deterministically protects timing
decisions.rejected: Live-animation screenshots or numeric contrast substitution

decisions.decision: Test literal authored content and optional-audio failure in the browser journey
decisions.why: Reveal refactoring must preserve escaping and remain functional when sound fails
decisions.rejected: Asset-string checks or audio call-count assertions alone

decisions.decision: Anchor reveal scheduling to the original start time while preserving 40ms row targets
decisions.why: Chained timers can accumulate scheduler drift and violate the 1.2-second 25-row acceptance bound
decisions.rejected: Allowing each timer callback delay to compound

decisions.decision: Use content-aware private reveal identities and retain completed container identity
decisions.why: Identical authoritative snapshots and reconnects must preserve both active progress and completed DOM, while changed text under the same navigation key must still replace and reveal
decisions.rejected: Unconditionally resetting render keys on every live-terminal projection

decisions.decision: Use generation-bearing opaque pattern IDs plus rendered board content as browser-local reveal identity
decisions.why: The public player projection already carries stable authoritative pattern IDs and complete board text, preserving progress without expanding the RPC schema
decisions.rejected: Atomic full-grid insertion or an additional public generation field

decisions.decision: Reveal complete row descriptors into persistent empty column shells through the shared reveal controller
decisions.why: This preserves deterministic two-column DOM order, keeps unrevealed targets absent, supports cancellation, and reuses established skip semantics
decisions.rejected: Character-by-character hacking markup or independent unmanaged timers

decisions.decision: Use stable generation identity plus coordinate-keyed mutable row snapshots
decisions.why: Dud removal mutates board text inside one authoritative generation and must preserve the existing reveal controller and row DOM
decisions.rejected: Including mutable column text in reveal identity, which restarts the full reveal

decisions.decision: Replace the queued descriptor row for an unrevealed dud target without appending it
decisions.why: The active reveal controller retains the descriptor and exposes the updated row only at its original turn
decisions.rejected: Reconciling pending content directly into the live DOM, which would expose interaction early

FR-001.title: The player experience MUST present every supported state within one consistent CRT visual shell.

FR-002.title: The CRT shell MUST provide a dark screen, green phosphor foreground, restrained glow, scanline texture, and edge darkening while preserving text legibility.

FR-003.title: Decorative CRT layers MUST cover the visible screen without receiving pointer or keyboard interaction.

FR-004.title: Connection feedback MUST remain visually dominant and readable without permanently replacing or mutating the underlying player state.

FR-005.title: Selection, focus, active, and hacking-hover feedback MUST preserve the exact historical color treatment and MUST be validated through approved visual snapshot baselines rather than a numeric contrast threshold.

FR-006.title: Screen flicker MUST use the historical six-second cycle with opacity 1 through 96%, .92 at 97%, 1 at 98%, .96 at 99%, and 1 at 100%.

FR-007.title: Cursor and pending-action indicators MUST use a discrete on/off presentation that remains independent of screen flicker.

FR-008.title: Newly opened folder rows, record lines, and command-output lines MUST reveal progressively in source order under normal motion settings.

FR-009.title: A replacement render MUST cancel any unfinished reveal associated with the replaced content.

FR-010.title: An unchanged content identity MUST NOT replay progressive reveal solely because another player-state field changed.
tests: tests/browser/crt-rendering.spec.mjs::25 rows reveal in order within 1.2 seconds and unchanged updates do not replay

FR-011.title: Pagination, viewport recalculation, and font-fit recalculation MUST NOT restart progressive reveal for already visible content.

FR-012.title: While a folder, record, or command page is progressively revealing, pressing any keyboard key MUST stop the active reveal, render the complete current page immediately, and consume that key without performing its normal action; normal keyboard handling MUST resume on the next key press.

FR-013.title: The visual shell and essential controls MUST remain usable without page-level scrolling across the supported compact, medium, and large viewport checks.
tests: tests/browser/crt-rendering.spec.mjs::CRT visual shell viewport state matrix

FR-014.title: CRT presentation behavior MUST remain local to the player experience and MUST NOT alter authoritative navigation, hacking, identity, broadcast, or persistence state.

FR-015.title: Optional audio availability or playback failure MUST NOT prevent the visual shell, animation fallback, or player interaction from working.

FR-016.title: The player experience MUST NOT expose or honor a reduced-motion mode that disables screen flicker, cursor blinking, pending-state pulsing, or other persistent CRT effects; reveal skipping applies only to the currently rendering page.

SC-006.title: All nine CRT presentation states remain readable and operable at all three supported viewports.
